A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an efficient algorithm for computing the exact gradient for the output weights of neural networks with sparse output targets.
we show how to train a deep network with very large sparse targets in the same time and memory complexity as training with a large sparse input.

we show how to efficiently compute a gradient of the loss with respect to the output weights and a backpropagation of the gradient with respect to the hidden layers for large sparse target vector, which has not been possible before.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while sparse input is a ubiquitous property of neural language models and word-embeddings that has been well-exploited for many years, it has not been so for sparse targets.
the problem of training large sparse networks with large sparse targets is no longer intractable.
it is possible to efficiently train large networks on large sparse targets.
